newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco doubts off-exchange copper stocks.
newsitem.headline: Codelco doubts off-exchange copper stocks.

text.p: Reports of large off-exchange copper stocks which have unnerved world markets are unlikely to be true, a top futures trading official for state-owned Chile mining firm Codelco, the world's largest producer, said on Thursday.

"We are buying cathodes in Europe and we know the situation is very tight. We have a subsidiary there, they buy 80,000 tonnes a year and the premiums ... everything reflects that the market is tight," Jorge Cristi, general manager of Codelco's futures market department, told Reuters in an interview at a copper conference.
"We are buying at a premium of $50, $70 Rotterdam basis for the whole year, so premiums are very high. And this was not only with one trader but with different traders," he said.
Copper markets in Britain and the United States were spooked Thursday by reports that as much as half a million tonnes of copper may be hidden in Rotterdam bonded warehouses.
Cristi also said that he did not believe the Chinese were presently active buyers in world copper markets: "We think that the market doesn't believe that the Chinese are really buying copper."
